transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-07 14:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Vogel (Bluehaven Head of Platform), Tom Greene (Bluehaven SRE Lead), Amir Khan (Bluehaven Procurement), Sofia Marin (Bluehaven Security)

Summary:
Quick check-in to align on renewal timing (current contract lapsing late Sep), Bluehaven interest in adding an EU on-prem/private pilot for data residency, capacity uplift (approx 2x committed throughput), and contract extension options. Agreed to run a short benchmark and for Redwood to send an amended SOW with pricing scenarios.

Topics discussed:
- Current usage and pain points (latency spikes for EU customers, burst handling)
- Private/EU on-prem pilot vs Dedicated EU capacity
- Pricing options for 12 month renewal vs 24 month commit
- Security artifacts: SOC2/ISO, KMS/HSM integration and audit log retention
- Technical benchmark plan and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you carving out time. quick roll call — we got, uh, Maya and Carlos from Redwood, and from Bluehaven Lena, Tom, Amir, Sofia — hi all.
[00:00:12] Lena: Hi, yes thanks, morning. we wanted to do a status check on the renewal and to talk through the EU onprem pilot that legal flagged.
[00:00:20] Maya: Totally — goal for today is sync on timing and the technical next steps, and then I can follow up with an SOW that has both hosted and private EU options.
[00:00:30] Tom: Quick context — our EU traffic has grown 45% q/q, and we're seeing p95 latencies climb during peak; right now we route everything to regional hosted which is fine but data residency is becoming a blocker for a couple of enterprise deals.
[00:00:45] Carlos: Got it. can you remind us of current committed throughput and typical sequence lengths? that shapes whether the onprem pilot needs dedicated GPUs or can run on a smaller dedicated cluster.
[00:00:55] Lena: We're currently committed to ~120k tokens/day, avg seq length 180, bursts to 4x for campaigns. target is to provision for about 250k tokens/day and keep headroom for bursts.
[00:01:10] Maya: So roughly 2x baseline + burst headroom — okay that helps. question for procurement: timeline expectations for renewal? Amir?
[00:01:20] Amir: We'd like contract signed before end of September. procurement needs two pricing scenarios: one for a 12-month renewal w/ EU hosted plus optional private pilot add-on, and one for a 24-month commitment with a discount. also need explicit SLAs for latency and provisioning time.
[00:01:36] Maya: Perfect — we'll include both in the doc. we'll also call out lead times for EU onprem provisioning; Carlos, what's realistic for a private EU pilot?
[00:01:46] Carlos: If it's onprem (customer managed infra) and we do the Redwood Private control plane, initial integration and onboarding — assuming network/VPN and KMS access are ready — could be 3-5 weeks for a minimal pilot (single rack / small cluster). for a fully managed private in a coloc or cloud VPC with dedicated nodes, 2-3 weeks if infra is already cleared.
[00:02:06] Sofia: From security: main ask is that keys stay in our HSM, and audit logs must be retained for 7 years for specific EU contracts. Also we need the option for e2e encryption of logs in transit.
[00:02:20] Carlos: We support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys; HSM handshake usually takes a couple of calls but it's supported. audit log retention is configurable — we'll surface retention options in the security doc we send.
[00:02:34] Tom: For the benchmark, we want to mirror real traffic shape — mix of short gen and 3 longer completion types. any recommendations on payloads?
[00:02:42] Carlos: We'll propose a test harness: 1) synthetic replay of 24h of peak traffic scaled down to a 3hr test window, 2) KV/cache warm-up step, 3) p50/p95/p99 latency and tail token throughput. we'll capture GPU metrics and token cost estimates.
[00:03:00] Lena: Nice. also want to understand cost delta between hosted and private — not just raw infra cost but the operational support overhead.
[00:03:08] Maya: We'll present a TCO view — break out infra, support, and integration labor. and show quantization/throughput tradeoffs that could lower unit cost.
[00:03:18] Amir: On the legal/compliance side we'll need data processing addendum updates for EU residency. is that something Redwood can update in the SOW?
[00:03:26] Maya: Yes, we can include DPA language and a private-region addendum. legal usually takes 1-2 weeks after SOW to review.
[00:03:34] Sofia: Important note — some EU customers require onprem or air-gapped options for PHI. can Redwood support an air-gapped deployment?
[00:03:42] Carlos: Air-gapped is possible, it's a different delivery track — on-site packaging and a heavier validation plan. that would add lead time and a professional services SKU, which we'll call out separately.
[00:03:55] Tom: ok, good to know. on latency — if we do EU private pilot, p95 should drop under 150ms for interactive traffic; can Redwood hit that?
[00:04:04] Carlos: Yes, with local KV cache warm and pinned model variants we can hit that. the key is sequence length and cache hit rate; we'll instrument traces during the benchmark.
[00:04:14] Lena: Any known limitations re: model versions and quantization for onprem? we've got strict accuracy requirements for a classifier.
[00:04:22] Carlos: We support standard quantized variants that we've verified; we'll produce a performance vs. quality matrix for the specific model family you use. Claudia (our model ops) usually runs a short eval to show any regression.
[00:04:35] Maya: wanted to call out competitive landscape — Lena, you mentioned Anthropic in an earlier note — customers often weigh latency/cost vs model fidelity. we'll highlight where Redwood's operational tooling and fallbacks help.
[00:04:48] Lena: Yeah Anthropic's latency on some benchmarks was lower in hosted but they don't offer the private onprem control plane we need.
[00:04:56] Amir: procurement also asked for payment terms options — net 30 vs net 45, and possibility of milestone invoices tied to pilot completion.
[00:05:04] Maya: We'll propose milestone-based billing for the pilot and standard net-30 for production commits.
[00:05:10] Sofia: security artifacts — please send SOC2 Type 2 report, ISO 27001 cert, and the KMS integration guide. we have a shared folder (bluehaven/security) where you can drop them.
[00:05:20] Maya: will do.
[00:05:22] Carlos: I'll lay out the benchmark steps in a doc and propose specific payloads — want to make sure we capture your KV/warm cache behavior. Tom, can you confirm endpoints and network egress constraints?
[00:05:31] Tom: yes, I'll share the network diagram and a sample of typical request shapes. also will share the prowler-like checklist we use for infra readiness.
[00:05:40] Maya: Great. high-level timeline proposal: SOW sent by Aug 10, benchmark week Aug 18-21, pilot provisioning soon after benchmark sign-off, contract signed end of September. does that match?
[00:05:52] Lena: That works for us, yes.
[00:05:54] Amir: one caveat — procurement wants the ability to pause additional spend if pilot uncovers major perf regressions. need a rollback clause.
[00:06:03] Maya: we'll include fallback terms and a remediation SLA in the SOW.
[00:06:07] Sofia: also note retention: 7 years for logs on certain datasets; make sure the SOW doesn't promise shorter retention for those.
[00:06:15] Maya: understood, we'll enumerate retention tiers.
[00:06:18] Carlos: any other technical blockers?
[00:06:20] Lena: nothing else on my side. just want to ensure the cost model is explicit especially around burst pricing.
[00:06:27] Maya: we'll add burst caps and a model for overage.
[00:06:30] Amir: final ask — include sample SLAs: provisioning time, p95 latency, and incident response times.
[00:06:36] Maya: noted. we'll include SLA table.
[00:06:40] (brief cross talk)
[00:07:00] Maya: ok great — recap quick: 1) Redwood sends SOW w/ two pricing scenarios by Aug 10; 2) Carlos to send benchmark plan and coordinate window (Aug 18 proposed); 3) Bluehaven to share network diagrams, QPS profile, and security folder access; 4) Redwood shares SOC2/ISO and KMS guide.
[00:07:20] Lena: good recap. thanks.
[00:07:22] Amir: thanks all.
[00:07:24] Sofia: thanks.
[00:07:30] Maya: we'll follow up in email with links and the calendar invite for the benchmark. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

References shared during call:
- Internal: Redwood benchmark plan (link sent after call)
- Security docs: SOC2/ISO placeholders (to be uploaded)
- Bluehaven shared folder: bluehaven/security (Sofia to grant access)

Keywords: renewal, EU onprem, private pilot, capacity uplift, SOW, benchmark, SOC2, KMS, audit logs, pricing scenarios
